questions.question: Consider the system $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}_t$, $t=0,1,2,\ldots$, with state $\boldsymbol{x}_t\in\mathbb{R}^n$, a fixed real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ and given forcing vectors $\boldsymbol{b}_t$. When is this system called homogeneous?
options: When $\boldsymbol{b}_0=\boldsymbol{0}$, whatever the later inputs are
When $\boldsymbol{x}_0=\boldsymbol{0}$, so the path starts at the origin
When the input is constant, $\boldsymbol{b}_t=\boldsymbol{b}$ for all $t$

questions.question: For the homogeneous system $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with real $n\times n$ matrix $A=(a_{ij})$, the solution is $\boldsymbol{x}_t=A^t\boldsymbol{x}_0$ with the matrix power $A^t$. For which class of matrices is $(A^t)_{ij}=a_{ij}^t$ guaranteed for all $i,j$ and $t\ge1$?
In the system $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with state $\boldsymbol{x}_t=(x_{1,t},\ldots,x_{n,t})^{\top}$ and real matrix $A=(a_{ij})$, what does the entry $a_{ij}$ measure?
options: The weight of today's $x_{i,t}$ in next period's $x_{j,t+1}$
The weight of $x_{i,t+1}$ in $x_{j,t+1}$ within the same period
The weight of today's $x_{j,t}$ in next period's $x_{i,t+1}$
The change $x_{i,t+1}-x_{i,t}$ caused by one unit of $x_{j,t}$

questions.question: For the homogeneous system $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$, the initial vector is an eigenvector: $\boldsymbol{x}_0=\boldsymbol{p}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$ with $A\boldsymbol{p}=\lambda\boldsymbol{p}$. What is $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ for every $t\ge0$?

Consider $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}_t$, $t=0,1,2,\ldots$, where the real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ is singular, the forcing sequence $(\boldsymbol{b}_t)$ is given and the initial vector $\boldsymbol{x}_0$ is given. How many solutions $(\boldsymbol{x}_t)_{t\ge0}$ are there?
options: None, because the solution formula requires the inverse $A^{-1}$
Infinitely many, one for each vector in the null space $\operatorname{Null}(A)$
Exactly one, but only if every $\boldsymbol{b}_t$ lies in $\operatorname{Col}(A)$
Exactly one, obtained by iterating the equation forward from $\boldsymbol{x}_0$

questions.question: For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_0=(1,0)^{\top}$, what is $\boldsymbol{x}_2$?
For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_0=(3,4)^{\top}$, which formula gives $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ for every $t\ge0$?

For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.25\\0&0.5\end{pmatrix}$ and constant input $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1)^{\top}$, which vector is the equilibrium $\boldsymbol{x}^*$, the constant solution with $\boldsymbol{x}^*=A\boldsymbol{x}^*+\boldsymbol{b}$?

The matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ has eigenvalue $3$ with eigenvector $(1,1)^{\top}$ and eigenvalue $1$ with eigenvector $(1,-1)^{\top}$. For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with $\boldsymbol{x}_0=(5,1)^{\top}$, what is the second component of $\boldsymbol{x}_t$?
The scalar equation $x_{t+2}=5x_{t+1}-6x_t$ is rewritten as a system $\boldsymbol{y}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{y}_t$ with state vector $\boldsymbol{y}_t=(x_{t+1},x_t)^{\top}$. Which matrix $A$ does this?

For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}$ with constant input $\boldsymbol{b}$, let $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ satisfy $(I-A)\boldsymbol{x}^*=\boldsymbol{b}$ and define the deviation $\boldsymbol{e}_t=\boldsymbol{x}_t-\boldsymbol{x}^*$. Which recursion does $\boldsymbol{e}_t$ satisfy?

A real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ has a repeated eigenvalue. For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$, when can every solution be written as $\boldsymbol{x}_t=\sum_{i=1}^n c_i\lambda_i^t\boldsymbol{p}_i$ with eigenpairs $(\lambda_i,\boldsymbol{p}_i)$ of $A$?
options: Exactly when $A$ still has $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors
Never, because this form needs $n$ distinct eigenvalues
Always, since a repeated eigenvalue simply appears twice in the sum
Exactly when $A$ is invertible, so that $P^{-1}$ exists

questions.question: A real $2\times2$ matrix $A$ has the nonreal eigenvalues $1\pm\mathrm{i}$. For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with a real initial vector $\boldsymbol{x}_0$, which statement about the vectors $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ is correct?
options: Each $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with $t\ge1$ has nonreal entries, inherited from the eigenvalues
No eigen-expansion exists, so $A^t$ has to be computed entrywise
Each $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ is real; the two complex eigen-terms are conjugates whose sum is real
Each $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ is real only when $(1\pm\mathrm{i})^t$ is real, i.e. $t$ a multiple of $4$

questions.question: The system $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}$ has $A=\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.25\\0.25&0.5\end{pmatrix}$, constant input $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1)^{\top}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_0=(5,3)^{\top}$. $A$ has eigenvalue $0.75$ with eigenvector $(1,1)^{\top}$ and eigenvalue $0.25$ with eigenvector $(1,-1)^{\top}$. What is the first component of $\boldsymbol{x}_t$ for $t\ge0$?
For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with the non-diagonalizable matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_0=(0,1)^{\top}$, what is $\boldsymbol{x}_3$?

For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}_t$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_0=\boldsymbol{0}$, there is a single input $\boldsymbol{b}_0=(0,1)^{\top}$ at time $0$ and $\boldsymbol{b}_t=\boldsymbol{0}$ for all $t\ge1$. What is $\boldsymbol{x}_3$?

Suppose $1$ is an eigenvalue of the real $n\times n$ matrix $A$. For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t+\boldsymbol{b}$ with constant $\boldsymbol{b}$, the equilibria are the solutions of $(I-A)\boldsymbol{x}^*=\boldsymbol{b}$. What is true of the set of equilibria?
options: It is always empty, as for the scalar case $a=1$ with $b\neq0$
It is empty or infinite, depending on whether $\boldsymbol{b}\in \operatorname{Col}(I-A)$
It is the single point $\boldsymbol{x}^*=\boldsymbol{0}$, since $I-A$ is singular
It is a single point whenever $A$ itself is invertible

questions.question: Two sequences $(\boldsymbol{x}_t)$ and $(\boldsymbol{y}_t)$ both solve $\boldsymbol{z}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{z}_t+\boldsymbol{b}$ with a constant input $\boldsymbol{b}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$, from different initial vectors. Which of the following sequences is guaranteed to solve the same forced equation?
For $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues are $1\pm\mathrm{i}$, and $\boldsymbol{x}_0=(1,0)^{\top}$, what is $\boldsymbol{x}_6$?

A solution of $\boldsymbol{x}_{t+1}=A\boldsymbol{x}_t$ with real $2\times2$ matrix $A$ is $\boldsymbol{x}_t=2^t(1,0)^{\top}+(-1)^t(1,1)^{\top}$ for all $t\ge0$. Which matrix $A$ produces this solution?
